results.fact: Which summit is the true high point
results.evidence: A detailed traverse trip report reaches the 'true summit' first from Cameron Pass after many false summits, then continues on the ridge to the Middle Peak (class 3-4 spots) and on to the East Peak. The main topo database, however, titles the 7,190 ft high point 'Mount Cameron - East Peak' (page itself not fetchable, title only from search). Wikipedia and PeakVisor give only 'triple-summit, 7,190 ft'. The naming conflict (which top is called East) cannot be settled with two agreeing sources, so the East/Middle/true labels in overview, waypoints[5].name/note, pro_tips[3] and approach_variants[0].baseFinding are left as is. (The beta's 'Middle/true summit' wording is removed under the difficulty fix without asserting either label.)

results.correct_value: The standard line is the long, gradual ridge climbed east from Cameron Pass (the peak's west ridge), not a southeast ridge/slope above Cameron Basin.
results.evidence: A traverse trip report climbs Cameron from Cameron Pass along 'a long gradual ridge', mostly class 1-2 over many false summits; peakery's ascent summary likewise goes basin -> Cameron Pass -> up the ridge with light scrambling. Cameron Pass lies due west of the summit (pass ~47.8257,-123.358; summit ~47.8258,-123.334, PeakVisor 47.8252,-123.328), so the ridge from the pass is the west ridge. The route NAME and aspect 'N' are out of scope (name not editable; no source for a single aspect value) and are left.

results.evidence: No outside source states a car-to-car gain, loss or one-way approach distance for Mount Cameron from Obstruction Point. Trail-loop figures found (Cameron Pass Trail 28.3 mi/8,110 ft; Cameron Basin loop 25.6 mi/7,959 ft; Cameron Creek loop 26.5 mi/7,654 ft) are for different hikes and disagree with each other and with the row's 9.3-9.9 mi one-way. Per rules gain_ft/loss_ft/dist_km are not recomputed.

results.evidence: One traverse report camped in upper Cameron Basin on a flat sandy spot in 'moonscape' moraine with no tree cover; another hiker describes a 'lush, marshy basin'. Neither supports 'old-growth, mossy', but no second source directly confirms the treeless camp, and NPS requires bear canisters park-wide (not because of missing trees), so no patch.

results.correct_value: The true summit is reached on Class 1-2 (Class 2) ground; Class 3-4 appears only on the traverse beyond it.
results.evidence: A traverse trip report says the climb from Cameron Pass is a long gradual ridge, mostly class 1-2 over false summits to the true summit, with class 3-4 spots only on the ridge on to the Middle Peak. Wikipedia gives the easiest route as class 2 scrambling. grade 'Class 2-3', the waypoint and the itinerary already agree; beta, pitch_detail and the three baseFinding texts are corrected.

results.evidence: Two independent road guides state Obstruction Point Road usually opens early/mid-July (one says mid-July) and closes mid-October; best_season, seasonal_guidance, access.closures and road.seasonalGate already say July. The season chip is set to Jul-Sep.

No outside source gives a camp-to-summit round-trip time for Mount Cameron's standard route. Note (discovered in the same place): the Day 2 schedule itself runs 6:00 AM to ~1:00 PM (7 h) against hours 5.5, so the itinerary is internally inconsistent as well; not patched without a source.

results.correct_value: Wilderness permit required; Grand and Badger Valleys (on the Obstruction Point approach) are a quota area; Royal Basin is a different drainage.
results.evidence: The NPS wilderness reservations page lists 'Grand and Badger Valleys' and 'Royal Basin/Royal Lake' as separate quota areas and does not list Cameron Basin; it says bear canisters are required in all wilderness camp areas. The Washington's National Park Fund permit guide also lists Grand Valley and Royal Lake as separate quota areas. The Royal Lake text is replaced with the Grand/Badger Valleys fact.
